question.text: A portfolio manager wants to replicate a NIFTY 500 index portfolio for a client, but several smallcap constituents trade thinly. Which indexing technique is most appropriate?

answer.text: Full replication — always preferred regardless of constituent liquidity
Sampling — replace illiquid constituents with similar liquid stocks
Buy and hold the top 50 stocks only, ignoring the rest of the index
Skip cash equities entirely and use only sector ETFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that sampling is used when full replication of a broad index like NIFTY 500 is difficult because of low-liquidity constituents and higher transaction costs, with the manager replacing some illiquid stocks with similar liquid stocks. The Trap: Full replication ignores the liquidity problem the workbook flags. Buying only the top 50 abandons the NIFTY 500 mandate. Substituting sector ETFs is not the indexing technique the workbook describes for this situation. Note: Sampling targets the same risk and return profile as full replication while accepting a small tracking error in exchange for lower transaction cost and easier execution.
